items.title: Lee Simpson (founder of Jefferson City Buzzards) Interview, 1948-06-09
items.who: Lee Simpson (founder of Jefferson City Buzzards)
items.q: we perched it from a Negro brick mason by the name of Monroe Wilson, who lived right around the corner from the club on Bellcastle between Law and Lunciation, and gave him $225 for the ground.

ctx.x: That is one of the incidents of the Lock's visit.

Dr. Dorman Church with rings in their nose. And when we struck Petit Avenue and Law Street, going up to Marfell's to make our formation, Brother Wilmer, my Brother Wilmer, jumped, there was a bunch of niggers, little niggers on the corner, and he jumped out and made like he got to grab one, and the nigger got to fits. And it was a time waking on to bring him to. Uh, Brother Simpson, maybe you can give us a few details on the time we paraded with a fire truck when you run into Brother Ziggler's garden with it.…
And he blocked them out at the New Orleans Ball Ball.
